q: 131. The maximum number of steps in a flight should generally be restricted to
explain: To prevent fatigue and ensure safety, a single flight of stairs is usually limited to 12 steps before a landing is required.

q: 132. The number of steps in a flight generally should not be less than
explain: A minimum of 3 steps is recommended to make the change in level obvious and prevent tripping.

q: 133. Sum of tread and rise must lie between
explain: The standard comfort rule for stairs is that (Rise + Tread) should be approximately 40 to 45 cm.

q: 134. Minimum width of landing should be
options: one fourth the width of stairs
explain: For safety and ease of turn, a landing must be at least as wide as the stair flight leading to it.

q: 135. In any good staircase, the maximum and minimum pitch respectively should be
explain: The ideal pitch (slope) for a comfortable stair is between 25° and 40°.

q: 136. The height between two floors is 3.00 m and riser is 15 cm. Assuming two flights between the floors, the number of treads will be
explain: Total risers = 300/15 = 20. In two flights with a landing, each flight has 10 risers. Since Treads = Risers - 1 per flight, total treads = (10-1) + (10-1) = 18.

q: 137. Half turn stairs are the stairs which change their direction through
explain: Half-turn stairs (like dog-legged stairs) reverse direction by 180 degrees.

q: 138. Doglegged stairs are
explain: Doglegged stairs are a specific type of half-turn stair where the two flights are contiguous with no well-hole between them.

q: 139. Nosing is the outer projecting edge of a
explain: The nosing is the rounded front edge of a tread that overhangs the riser below.

q: 140. The lower most horizontal piece of a shutter is known as
explain: The horizontal members of a door or window shutter are called rails; the lowest one is the bottom rail.

q: 141. From the point of view of maximum day light, the windows in a room should be located on
explain: In the northern hemisphere, northern light is preferred as it provides steady, diffused daylight throughout the day without harsh solar heat gain.

q: 142. The minimum number of holdfasts recommended on each side of a door frame and a window frame respectively are
explain: Standard practice requires 3 holdfasts for door heights and 2 for window heights on each side to ensure stability.

q: 143. The opening left in flat roofs for lightings purposes is called
explain: A skylight is an opening in a roof covered with glass or plastic to admit natural light.

q: 144. The suitable door for entrance in an air-conditioned building is a
explain: Revolving doors act as an airlock, minimizing the exchange of indoor and outdoor air to maintain HVAC efficiency.

q: 145. While classifying the building, cinema hall should be classified as
explain: Buildings where large numbers of people gather for entertainment or assembly are classified as Public (Assembly) buildings.

q: 146. The building of an Engineering college should be classified as
explain: Buildings used for instructional purposes are classified as Educational buildings.

q: 147. The live load on the floors of residential buildings, hospital wards, private sitting room in hostels should be
explain: The standard design live load for residential areas and private rooms is 2.0 kN/m² (approx 200 Kg/m²).

q: 148. The load of furniture stored in a building is termed as
explain: Live loads (imposed loads) are movable loads, such as people, furniture, and movable equipment.

q: 149. While calculating the dead load of a building, the weight of brick masonry is taken as
explain: The unit weight of common brick masonry is standardly taken as 19.2 kN/m³ (approx 1920 Kg/m³).

q: 150. The safe bearing capacity for hard rock should be
explain: Hard, massive rock has very high bearing capacity, typically exceeding 250 t/m² (2500 kN/m²).

q: 151. Generally for a column in a workshop using Gantry cranes, the foundation to be used should be
explain: Grillage foundations are used for heavy isolated column loads to spread the pressure over a larger area of soil.

q: 152. For an ordinary double storey building, the type of foundation to be used should be
explain: Spread footings are the most common and economical choice for low-rise residential structures on stable soil.

q: 153. While constructing a bridge upon a river, the foundation to be adopted in pillars should be
explain: Well (Caisson) foundations are standard for bridge piers in rivers due to their ability to withstand scour and provide high load capacity.

q: 154. For a bridge pier, in very deep water the foundation to be used should be
explain: In very deep water where a standard well foundation is difficult, a pneumatic or floating caisson is used.

q: 155. Maximum size of aggregates used in a DPC is about
explain: Damp Proof Courses (DPC) use a thin layer of concrete/mortar, requiring small aggregates, typically capped at 10mm.

q: 156. When the two blocks of stone have a tendency to be pulled apart in the direction of their lengths, then the type of joint to be used should be
explain: A cramped joint uses a metal 'cramp' to tie two stones together, preventing them from being pulled apart by tension.

q: 157. While laying bricks in a wall, frog of the brick must be kept
explain: The frog (indentation) is kept upward so that it fills with mortar, creating a mechanical 'key' for the course above.

q: 158. In a single day the maximum height of masonry to be raised should not be more than
explain: Masonry height is limited to 1.5m per day to prevent the fresh mortar in lower courses from being crushed by excessive weight before setting.

q: 159. If after every three or four stretchers, one header is used in a brick masonry wall, then the bond so formed will be called as
explain: English Garden Wall bond consists of several courses of stretchers followed by one course of headers (typically 3:1 or 5:1 ratio).

q: 160. The wall constructed along the slopes to protect the slopes of cutting from the adverse effect of atmosphere are called as
explain: Breast walls are designed specifically to prevent the weathering or 'slipping' of natural soil slopes, whereas retaining walls are meant to resist the active earth pressure of a backfill.

q: 161. Dry bricks are recommended in brick masonry when the mortar used is
explain: For cement and lime mortars, bricks must be soaked to prevent them from absorbing water from the mortar; however, with mud mortar, dry bricks are used to avoid over-softening the mud.

q: 162. The most important tool used by a mason in laying of bricks while constructing a wall is
explain: The trowel is the primary tool for lifting, spreading, and leveling mortar, as well as for 'tapping' bricks into their correct position.

q: 163. The best and the most common material to be used as damp proofing material is
explain: Bitumen is highly effective, flexible, and impermeable, making it the most common material for horizontal and vertical DPC layers.

q: 164. To facilitate draining off rain water from the coping, sills, sunshades, a groove is cut on the underside of these and this groove is known as
explain: Throating (or a drip groove) breaks the surface tension of water, forcing it to drop off the edge rather than running back toward the wall face.

q: 165. To protect the top of a parapet wall from the action of rain water, it is provided with a special course and that course if known as
explain: Coping is a waterproof covering (usually stone, brick, or concrete) placed on the top of an exposed wall to shed water.

q: 166. In a fact roofed building, the roof is made water proof by coating hot bitumen and this coating is done at the rate of
explain: The standard rate for a single coat of hot bitumen for waterproofing a flat roof surface is 1.65 to 1.67 Kg per square meter.

q: 167. The width of rebate provided in a door frame is equal to the width of the shutter whereas depth of the rebate provided should be
explain: The rebate depth (usually 12-13 mm) is standard to ensure the door shutter sits flush and provides a seal against light and sound.

q: 168. Generally in latrines, kitchens and bathrooms the door used is from the type of
options: partly glazed and partly panelled door
explain: Flush doors are preferred for wet areas because they are easy to clean, offer no crevices for dirt or moisture, and can be easily made waterproof.

q: 169. In a panelled door, the rails fixed in between the lock rail and top rail are called as
explain: The frieze rail is the intermediate horizontal member located specifically between the top rail and the lock rail.

q: 170. Generally the thickness of rails and styles adopted in a door frame is
explain: For standard domestic doors, a thickness of 30mm to 40mm (3-4 cm) provides the necessary structural rigidity without being excessively heavy.

q: 171. In a residential building, the width of a door cannot be less than
explain: While internal doors for bathrooms can be 0.75m, the general standard for habitable rooms in a residential building is 0.9m to allow for furniture and occupant movement.

q: 172. As compared to the floor area of a room, the glass area in a window should not be less than
explain: For adequate daylighting, building codes typically require the window glass area to be at least 1/10th (10%) of the floor area.

q: 173. A horizontal member fixed in door or window frame for the separation of fan light is known as
explain: A transom is the horizontal structural beam that separates a door from a window above it (the fanlight).

q: 174. The horizontal member forming the bottom of the frame is called as
explain: The sill is the lowest horizontal part of the window or door frame, designed to shed water away from the opening.

q: 175. The window provided on the sloping roof a building is called as
explain: A dormer window is a vertical window that projects from a sloping roof, creating extra headroom and light in an attic.

q: 176. The projection of tread beyond the riser is 'called as
explain: Nosing is the rounded edge of the tread that extends over the riser to provide more foot space and improve safety.

q: 177. The extreme support of a hand railing provided at the top and bottom of a flight is known as
explain: A newel post is the heavy vertical post at the start or end of a stair flight that provides structural anchoring for the handrail.

q: 178. The head room in a staircase should not be less than
explain: The minimum vertical clearance (headroom) measured from the pitch line to the ceiling must be 2.1m to prevent tall users from hitting their heads.

q: 179. While designing a stair, the product of rise and going is approximately kept equal to
explain: One of the standard rules for comfortable stairs is (Rise in cm x Going in cm) ≈ 400 to 450. Option 420 is the most common target.

q: 180. The under surface of stair is called as
explain: The soffit refers specifically to the exposed underside of any architectural element, including stairs, arches, or cornices.

q: 181. The additional support given to the nosing in a wooden stair is known as
explain: Scotia is a concave molding placed under the nosing of a tread to strengthen the joint and provide a finished look.

q: 182. In a stair, the ratio of the vertical distance covered and the horizontal distance occupied by a flight is called as
explain: Gradient is the ratio of Rise to Going (Rise/Going), defining the steepness of the flight.

q: 183. In a stair the best and most suitable position for providing winders is
explain: Providing winders at the bottom of a stair is safer and more aesthetically pleasing than placing them at the top, where they pose a greater trip hazard.

q: 184. The width of stair in a residential building cannot be less than
explain: A minimum of 80cm to 90cm is required to allow for one person to comfortably ascend or carry items.

q: 185. When both the flights in a stair run at right angles to each other, then that stair is classified as
explain: A quarter-turn stair changes direction by 90 degrees, usually at a landing.

q: 186. If landing is not to be counted then the number of treads as compared to risers in a stair are
explain: In a single flight, the last step up lands on the floor level, meaning there is always one less tread than there are risers (T = R - 1).

q: 187. Generally a 10 cm thick layer of sand is provided in the base and its purpose is
options: to avoid forming of pot holes
explain: Sand layers provide drainage (dampness), uniform pressure distribution (cushion), and prevent capillary action that leads to floor damage.

q: 188. Generally a layer in between the base and topping is used in some of the floors. This layer is named as under layer and the floors in which this layer is used are
explain: Terrazzo flooring consists of a decorative top layer and a plain cement concrete 'under layer' for structural support.

q: 189. The narrow strips of wood or bands of plaster laid on the floor to act as guides for bringing whole of the work to a true and even surface are termed as
explain: Screeds are long, straight strips used as gauges to ensure the floor topping is perfectly level and uniform.

q: 190. Brick floors are recommended to be used at
explain: Brick flooring is durable, cheap, and easy to repair, making it ideal for warehouses (godowns) and heavy storage areas.

q: 191. The stones used in flagstone flooring are rectangular square in shape and have thickness of
explain: Standard flagstones are typically 3cm to 5cm thick to provide sufficient strength without excessive weight.

q: 192. Flag stone floor is recommended to be used at
explain: Because it is natural, durable, and hard-wearing, flagstone is used in a wide variety of high-traffic and outdoor locations.

q: 193. While laying cement concrete floor, the floor is divided into small panels. For better results side of the panel should not exceed in lengths by
explain: To prevent shrinkage cracks in concrete flooring, panels are usually restricted to 1.5m to 2m in length.

q: 194. The thickness of terrazzo mix in Terrazzo floors should be approximately
explain: The decorative terrazzo topping layer is generally 6mm to 12mm thick, laid over a concrete base.

q: 195. While grinding the terrazzo floor, final cutting is done by the Carborundum stone of Number
explain: Higher grit numbers indicate finer stones; No. 120 is used for the final polishing stage to achieve a smooth finish.
